steps.description: 5 vertices, 6 weighted edges. First a DFS lists the vertices in topological order: a vertex is pushed only after everything it points to.
topoSort(0): mark 0 visited, then explore every vertex it points to first.
topoSort(1): mark 1 visited, then explore every vertex it points to first.
topoSort(2): mark 2 visited, then explore every vertex it points to first.
topoSort(3): mark 3 visited, then explore every vertex it points to first.
topoSort(4): mark 4 visited, then explore every vertex it points to first.
Every successor of vertex 4 is already on the stack, so push 4 on top.
Every successor of vertex 3 is already on the stack, so push 3 on top.
Every successor of vertex 2 is already on the stack, so push 2 on top.
Every successor of vertex 1 is already on the stack, so push 1 on top.
Every successor of vertex 0 is already on the stack, so push 0 on top.
The stack holds a topological order, top first: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]. Every distance starts at infinity except the source: distance[0] = 0.
Pop 0. Every edge into it came from a vertex earlier in the order, so distance[0] = 0 is final. Relax its outgoing edges.
0 -> 1 costs 0 + 2 = 2, better than infinity: distance[1] = 2.
0 -> 2 costs 0 + 4 = 4, better than infinity: distance[2] = 4.
Pop 1. Every edge into it came from a vertex earlier in the order, so distance[1] = 2 is final. Relax its outgoing edges.
1 -> 2 costs 2 + 1 = 3, better than 4: distance[2] = 3.
1 -> 3 costs 2 + 7 = 9, better than infinity: distance[3] = 9.
Pop 2. Every edge into it came from a vertex earlier in the order, so distance[2] = 3 is final. Relax its outgoing edges.
2 -> 3 costs 3 + 3 = 6, better than 9: distance[3] = 6.
Pop 3. Every edge into it came from a vertex earlier in the order, so distance[3] = 6 is final. Relax its outgoing edges.
3 -> 4 costs 6 + 2 = 8, better than infinity: distance[4] = 8.
Pop 4. Every edge into it came from a vertex earlier in the order, so distance[4] = 8 is final. Relax its outgoing edges.
Return distance = [0, 2, 3, 6, 8].
